title: Minimum Operations to Exceed Threshold Value II
statement:
You get an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. One operation takes the two smallest values of `nums`, call them `x <= y`, deletes both of them, and puts the single value `2 * x + y` back into the array (where it goes does not matter). An operation is only possible while `nums` holds at least two elements.

Return the fewest operations needed until every element of `nums` is at least `k`. The input is built so that this state can always be reached.
constraints: Some number of operations always makes every element at least k
notes:
## Intuition

The rule itself says which two numbers to combine, so there is nothing to choose: the answer is just how many times the rule fires before the smallest value reaches `k`. Re-sorting the array after every step simulates it correctly but costs O(n² log n). The process only ever asks for "the smallest" and "the next smallest", which is exactly what a min-heap serves in O(log n).

## Approach

1. Push every value of `nums` into a min-heap `heap`.
2. While the top of the heap (the current minimum) is below `k`, perform one operation.
3. Pop the smallest value `x`, then the next smallest `y`; since `x <= y`, the new value is `2 * x + y`.
4. Push the new value back and count the step in `operations`.
5. When the minimum is at least `k`, every value is, so return `operations`.

The guarantee means the heap never runs out of a second element while its minimum is still below `k`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 11, 10, 1, 3]`, `k = 10`. The heap minimum is `1 < 10`: pop `x = 1`, `y = 2`, push `4` (heap holds `3, 4, 10, 11`). The minimum `3 < 10`: pop `x = 3`, `y = 4`, push `10` (heap holds `10, 10, 11`). Now the minimum is `10`, not below `k`, so the answer is `operations = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n): building the heap is n pushes and each operation does three O(log n) heap steps, with at most n − 1 operations.
- Space: O(n) for the heap.

## Pitfalls

- Check only the minimum: once it is at least `k`, all others are too.
- The pair is the two smallest values *after* earlier merges, so a sorted copy of the input taken once is not enough on its own; merged values must rejoin the pool.
- In Java or C, `2 * x + y` can pass 2^31 (`x` and `y` reach 10^9), so use 64-bit integers.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `heap` | min-heap holding the current values of the array |
| `push`, `pop` | insert a value / remove and return the minimum, keeping the heap order |
| `operations` | number of operations done so far |
| `x`, `y` | the smallest and second smallest values being merged |

narration.34: Keep operating while the smallest value is still below k; if it is not, nothing else is.
